data: Inspired by the farm-to-table concept, the garden-to-glass movement highlights cocktails and zero-proof drinks made with locally sourced herbs, edible flowers, fruits, and vegetables, bringing seasonal flavor and a wellness boost

Everyone has one, a secret stash of food tucked in a drawer or the refrigerator for just-in-case moments, whether it’s soy sauce packets from takeout or a favorite chocolate bar for when the day calls for it

Fricy blends “fruity” and “spicy,” a 2026 food trend pairing sweet fruit with chili heat, showing up in spicy margaritas, snack toppings, and glazes like pork with charred pineapple, a next step after 2025’s “swicy”

Better known as Turkish delight, lokum is a classic confection from late 1700s Istanbul, made from sugar and starch and often flavored with rosewater or citrus, traditionally served with coffee or tea
A bouquet garni is a bundle of fresh herbs, traditionally parsley, thyme, and bay leaf, tied together with string or wrapped in cheesecloth to flavor soups, stews, stocks, and sauces

Trail mix is often called gorp, short for “Good Ol’ Raisins and Peanuts,” a hiker’s classic handful of nuts, dried fruit, and chocolate—and yes, many of us were today years old when we learned what gorp actually stands for

Maison Pickle, a New York City institution, has gone viral for its 24-layer pickle cake, pairing sweet cake and creamy frosting with pickle rinds, topped with sliced pickles, a surprising sweet-savory combo that somehow works
Wedding and celebration cakes are built in tiers — each layer baked and finished separately, then assembled into a showstopping centerpiece

An interactive crowd favorite at NYC's Spot Dessert Bar comes disguised as a potted plant with Oreo “soil,” whipped cream, chiffon cake, and strawberries, then gets “watered” with milk tea before digging in

Tracing back to the 1800s wine cobbler, frosé is a chilled wine-and-fruit drink served over crushed ice, and because alcohol doesn’t freeze solid, it keeps its signature slushy texture, making it a perfect warm-weather sip for Mother’s Day

French for “small ovens,” petits fours are bite-size confections traditionally baked in the residual heat of bread ovens, creating dainty delicacies—a sweet little celebration as Phoodle turns four today
